projects.name: InCloseMail
projects.description: Desktop email for personal inboxes and Microsoft 365 business accounts.
projects.tagline: An Outlook alternative built for the desktop.
projects.featureText: Use it with personal inboxes and Microsoft 365 business accounts. Free for personal email, with paid plans for business accounts.
projects.longDescription:
InCloseMail was checked against classic Outlook screen by screen: the ribbon, folder pane, reading pane and To-Do Bar, Outlook's keyboard shortcuts and right-click menus, .pst import and export, rules and Quick Steps, calendar, people and tasks, shared mailboxes and Microsoft 365 Groups.

It adds things Outlook doesn't have: AI agents such as Claude can read and draft mail in the mailboxes you choose, Clean Up My Inbox sorts thousands of messages into groups you can act on at once, you can change any keyboard shortcut, and it keeps working offline during a Microsoft 365 outage.

It is free forever for Outlook.com, Hotmail, Live and other personal Microsoft accounts. Microsoft 365 work accounts will cost $3 per user per month ($36 a year) after the beta, and are free during it. It runs on 64-bit Windows 10 (version 1809 or later) and Windows 11.

projects.name: DesktopWiki
projects.description: A wiki for internal docs and team knowledge, with a free single-user tier.
projects.tagline: A team wiki that runs on your own PC.
projects.featureText: Spaces, a page tree and a visual editor, plus a password manager, with no server or cloud account to set up. Free for one person, with paid plans for families and teams.
projects.longDescription:
DesktopWiki gives a family or small team spaces, a page tree and a visual editor, the way classic team wikis work, plus a password manager for everyone's logins. You install it on one Windows PC, and everyone else opens it in a browser on a phone or another computer.

There is no server, database or cloud account to set up: the whole wiki lives in one file you can back up by copying it. It can import from Confluence and can be opened up for use away from home.

It is free for one person. Family (up to 6 people) is $49 a year, Team (up to 18) $99 and Business (up to 60) $199, on sale after the beta, with every feature in every plan. The host PC needs 64-bit Windows 10 (version 1809 or later) or Windows 11.

projects.name: macshot
projects.alternative: Alternative to the macOS screenshot tool
projects.description: Capture, annotate, and record your screen. Includes scrolling capture and text recognition.
projects.longDescription:
macshot lives in the Mac menu bar. One hotkey freezes the screen so you can select a region, mark it up with arrows, text, shapes, numbered markers or blur, and copy it straight to the clipboard.

It also records the screen as MP4 or GIF with system audio and microphone, stitches scrolling captures into one tall image, reads text with OCR, can auto-redact emails, phone numbers and card numbers, and uploads to Google Drive, imgbb or any S3-compatible storage. It is a native Swift and AppKit app, also installable with Homebrew (brew install --cask macshot).
projects.builtWithAI: The macshot repo includes CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md instruction files for AI coding agents, and its commit history shows AI help: 37 of its 1,052 commits (checked 2026-11-21) are co-authored by Claude and 5 by Cursor. Most of the code is credited to its developer, sw33tLie.

projects.name: Locode
projects.description: Build React web apps from prompts using local Ollama models on an Apple Silicon Mac.
projects.longDescription:
Describe an app in plain English and Locode generates a complete React, Tailwind and Vite project, tests it with Playwright, fixes errors and lets you keep refining it with follow-up prompts. Everything runs on your own machine through Ollama, so there are no API keys or subscriptions.

The ready-made download is a DMG for Apple Silicon Macs. It can also be run from source with Python and Node.

projects.name: Glance
projects.description: Host and share previews of pages built by coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor.
projects.longDescription:
Glance lets a coding agent publish a page, dashboard or app to a live URL with one command (glance deploy). You leave comments on the page in the browser, much like in a Google Doc, and the agent reads them and fixes the page.

You host it yourself on Cloudflare's free tier. It works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Cline, Aider or any agent that can run a shell command, every link needs a login, and optional Slack notifications tell you about new comments.
projects.builtWithAI: Glance's commit history shows it was built mostly with Claude: 206 of its 251 commits (checked 2026-11-21) are co-authored by Claude models.

projects.name: FreeFlow
projects.description: Free voice dictation for your computer. Speak and it types for you, with no monthly subscription.
projects.builtWithAI: Zach Latta's original README (February 2026) said he "vibe-coded" FreeFlow over a weekend. The project keeps an AGENTS.md file for AI coding agents, and 97 of its 511 commits (checked 2026-11-21) are co-authored by Claude.
projects.longDescription:
Hold the Fn key, talk, and FreeFlow types what you said into whatever text field you are in. It cleans up filler words and spelling using nearby app context and your own vocabulary list, and Edit Mode can rewrite selected text from a spoken instruction such as "make this shorter".

It uses a free Groq API key by default, or any OpenAI-compatible provider including local models through Ollama or LM Studio. There is no FreeFlow server. It works on Apple Silicon and Intel Macs.

projects.name: Open Source Barware
projects.alternative: Alternative to paid bar inventory software
projects.description: Local-first bar inventory software for counting stock and tracking usage, licensed GPLv3.
projects.longDescription:
Walk your shelves and say what you see ("Tito's, half. Jameson, full.") and Open Source Barware builds the count sheet, prices every bottle and tells you what's short and what to reorder. Import last week's sales from your POS and it flags bottles that came up short.

It runs on your own Mac or Windows laptop, works without internet or AI (AI is optional, for reading invoice photos), counts in English or Spanish and can run several locations. There is a sample bar to try in the browser. It is free with no paid tier, under GPLv3.
projects.builtWithAI: The maker says AI is what let people from the bar trade build the tool themselves. The GitHub repo keeps CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md files for AI coding agents, and 56 of its 249 commits (checked 2026-11-22) are co-authored by Claude.

projects.name: Davit
projects.description: A native Mac app for running and managing Linux containers on Apple silicon, built on Apple's own container platform.
projects.longDescription:
Davit is a SwiftUI app for Apple's container platform, which runs each Linux container as a lightweight VM. It has a dashboard, container lists with live CPU and memory, logs, stats charts, a file browser and terminal for each container, image pulls and builds, volumes, networks, local DNS and Compose file import.

It needs an Apple silicon Mac with macOS 15 or newer, and installs Apple's container platform for you on first launch if it is missing. It is also available through Homebrew (brew install wouterdebie/tap/davit).

projects.name: OpenTodo
projects.description: A free, self-hosted to-do app with plain-language quick add, time blocking and shared lists, on the web, iPhone and Android.
projects.longDescription:
Type a task the way you say it ("Call Sarah next Wed 3pm #work p1") and OpenTodo sets the date, project and priority. Today shows what is due, you can drag tasks onto a day or week calendar to block out time, and Focus runs a Pomodoro or countdown timer that logs time to the task. Lists can be shared with family or a team, and it works offline.

You run the server yourself (Docker, a single binary for Windows, Mac or Linux, Unraid, Home Assistant and more) or rent a hosted copy from PikaPods. There is an iPhone and iPad app in the App Store and an Android APK. Everything is free, with no paid tier.

It needs an Apple silicon Mac running macOS 14 to 26. On macOS 27 it can't hide icons and points you to the system's own menu bar settings instead. The project is now community-maintained. Also available with Homebrew (brew install --cask sane-apps/tap/sanebar).

AI is optional: it can use Ollama offline, or Claude and OpenAI with your own key. Plugins run in a sandbox and follow an Obsidian-compatible API. It is built on Tauri, so the installer is about 10 MB.

projects.description: A free 2D and 3D CAD app with the command line, snaps, layers and dimensions drafters know, reading and writing DXF and DWG, for Windows, Mac, Linux, FreeBSD and the web, from the ArtCraft suite. Early development.
projects.longDescription:
CADCraft follows the classic drafting workflow: type a command such as LINE, click points or enter coordinates, and use object snaps, polar tracking, ortho, grips and right-click to repeat. It reads and writes DXF natively (R12 through 2018) and opens and saves DWG (R13 through 2018) through the open-source acadrust library, with SVG and PNG export. Its README calls it "in early, fast development"; release builds (v0.8.0 on 2026-11-22) are code-signed for Windows and macOS.

projects.name: Clean Your TV
projects.alternative: Alternative to the stock Google TV home screen
projects.description: Strips the ads, tracking and preloaded bloat from an Android TV or Google TV over Wi-Fi and swaps in a clean, Apple TV-style home screen. No root, nothing uninstalled, and one command undoes it all.
projects.longDescription:
Android TVs have the same debug bridge as Android phones. Clean Your TV uses it over Wi-Fi to back up your settings, switch off the maker's telemetry, ad services, sponsored rows and preloaded apps (switched off, not deleted), and install a small native launcher as the home screen. Its lists cover 504 TV models from 138 brands.

The usual way to run it is to hand the project's prompt to a coding assistant such as Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI on a computer on the same Wi-Fi; it finds the bloat on your TV and asks before touching anything you might use. projects.name: Tower of Time
projects.description: A tower defense game where you can rewind time: build turrets, manage energy, and when the waves break through, roll the clock back and try a new plan. Free to play in your browser.
projects.longDescription: Made for Beginner's Jam Summer 2025. Choose from basic turrets, sniper towers, slowdown towers and splash damage towers, and spend energy both on building and on rewinding. It plays with keyboard or gamepad.
projects.builtWithAI: The README calls it a vibe coding proof of concept: about 95% of the code was written by AI, using Augment Code and Cursor with Claude Sonnet 4 as the main model (plus some OpenAI o3 and Claude Opus 4). The prompts are published in the repo.

projects.name: Game Master Claude
projects.description: Turns Claude Code into a persistent game master for text role-playing campaigns, with lasting memory, real dice rolls and a world that keeps moving between sessions.
projects.longDescription:
Start a new world with /new-game, where a questionnaire shapes a custom setting and ruleset, or import a PDF of a book you own and step into it. The harness keeps a campaign journal, a custom rulebook and a living world, and Claude narrates, rolls the dice and runs the table.

You need Claude Code. The install script sets up everything on macOS and Linux.
projects.builtWithAI: Built for Claude Code and largely with it. Checked 2026-11-22: 104 of 176 commits are co-authored by Claude.

projects.name: Sakura Fantasy
projects.description: A boat journey down a Japanese river valley in any season and at any hour, rendered live in your browser: cherry trees, a drum bridge, a pagoda village, a bamboo gorge and a tunnel of torii.
projects.longDescription: You sit in a reed-roofed river boat while a boatman sculls you downstream, then the season turns and the journey begins again. Watch, or take the camera and stop to look around. It uses three.js and WebGL 2 with no game engine, and was featured in Ruan Yifeng's weekly and the Codrops Creative Hub. From the maker of Neon Zenith.
projects.builtWithAI: The README says it was built with Claude Code: the maker set the direction and reviewed every pass, and the model wrote the code, the shaders, the Blender asset scripts and the audio build.
